member.name: T:STAR_DOM.Web.DeliverySweepPage
member.summary: POST-only endpoint that runs the delivery sweep. Called by the scheduled GitHub Action, never by a browser.
member.remarks:
This page is deliberately not part of the site's session/CSRF machinery. It has no user, no cookie and no form: the caller is a cron job holding a shared secret, so the CSRF check has to be bypassed for this one exact path (see Global.asax.vb) and the request is authenticated by the DELIVERY_SWEEP_TOKEN header instead.
Three things are load-bearing: 1. The token comes from the environment, never from git. A secret in the repository is a secret everyone has. 2. A request with no token configured on the server is REFUSED (503) rather than allowed. Failing open would turn a forgotten environment variable into an unauthenticated endpoint that closes orders. 3. The comparison is constant-time, and the mismatching request is logged with the same Context the CSRF guard uses, so a probe looks the same as any other blocked request in AppErrors.
GET returns 405 rather than running anything: a sweep changes orders, and a method a crawler, a prefetcher or a link can trigger must never do that.

member.name: T:STAR_DOM.Services.CommissionLedgerService
member.summary: The studio's earnings ledger: one row per order, held until the parcel is confirmed received, voided if the order is refunded.
member.remarks:
This is a record, not a payment rail. There is no gateway in this application that could move money, and there is no attempt to fake one -- the same reason Orders.REFUNDED records a decision rather than performing a refund. The value here is that the question "has the studio actually earned this sale" has an answer that can be looked up, and that a refund after release is visible as a reversal rather than quietly disappearing.
The state machine is deliberately small, and every edge is one-way: HELD -> RELEASED (the customer confirmed the parcel arrived) HELD -> VOID (refunded before confirmation; nothing to reverse) RELEASED -> VOID (refunded after confirmation; Reversed = TRUE) Nothing moves out of RELEASED or VOID, so a retried sweep or a second refund record cannot inflate the books.

member.name: M:STAR_DOM.Services.CommissionLedgerService.ReleaseForOrder(STAR_DOM.Models.Order,System.String)
member.summary: Release the earning because the order is now RECEIVED.
member.remarks: Accrues first, then releases. That order matters and is not belt-and-braces: the release is a guarded UPDATE on a HELD row, so if the accrual never happened the release matches nothing and quietly does nothing -- the order becomes RECEIVED with no earning recorded anywhere. Delivery is normally the accrual point, but a delivered order can predate the ledger, and the sweep closes orders it did not itself deliver. Ensuring the row first makes "release on RECEIVED" true on every path that can reach RECEIVED, and EnsureHeld is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so an already-accrued row is untouched ---- no double commission.

Both are attempted without knowing which applies, because each is guarded on its own starting state and a mismatch is a no-op rather than an error.

member.name: M:STAR_DOM.Services.OrderService.OpenDispute(System.Int32,System.String)

The parcel may well have arrived and nobody has decided yet, and an order in that state must not read as either finished or refunded. member.name: M:STAR_DOM.Services.OrderService.ResolveDispute(System.Int32,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Close a dispute as RECEIVED, REFUNDED or RESHIP. Admin only.
member.remarks: The three outcomes are deliberately blunt. There is no reviewer queue and no partial state: someone has to look at the parcel and say what happened to it, and each of those three is a real answer. REFUNDED records that decision only -- the studio hands the money back over the phone or in person, because there is no gateway here that could move it by itself.

member.name: M:STAR_DOM.Services.OrderService.StudioMarkReceived(System.Int32,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Mark an order received on the customer's behalf. Admin only, and requires a reason, a proof of delivery already on file, and the admin's password.
member.remarks:
This exists for the real case: the customer tells the studio over the phone that the parcel arrived and never presses the button. Refusing would only push people back to arguing with the courier. What it must not be is silent -- so ReceiptSource records STUDIO and the reason is mandatory, leaving a plain answer to "why does this order say received when nobody clicked anything".
The locked spec requires POD + password for this path. An order without a proof of delivery cannot be closed by the studio on the customer's behalf.

member.name: M:STAR_DOM.Services.OrderService.SaveProofOfDelivery(System.Int32,System.Byte[],System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Record the courier outcome and proof of delivery for an order. Admin only.
member.remarks: Saving a POD does NOT close the order. It is evidence, and evidence is not a decision: the customer normally confirms receipt, and the dispute path still exists for when the evidence is wrong. Coupling the two would mean the studio could end an order unilaterally by uploading a screenshot, which is exactly the power this design is meant to take away.

member.name: M:STAR_DOM.Services.OrderService.RecordRefund(System.Int32,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Record a refund for an order. Admin only. The order status becomes REFUNDED (not CANCELLED), the IG reference is recorded, and the audit trail captures the reason. The money itself moves outside the system -- this records the decision, it does not perform a refund.
member.remarks:
The locked spec: "admin 'Record a refund' + reason + IG ref -> REFUNDED (not CANCELLED). receipt: existing OR marked refunded. commission: clawback. void commission row, flag reversal. No money moves."
Each of those three is honoured literally: - REFUNDED, never CANCELLED. Cancelling an order and refunding one are different facts, and writing CANCELLED over a paid order loses the record that money actually changed hands. - The official receipt is KEPT and stamped refunded. It cannot be re-issued (UNIQUE(PaymentId)) and it must not be deleted: the sale genuinely happened and the BIR record of it survives the refund. - The studio's earning is voided. If it had already been released when the customer confirmed receipt, the row is voided AND flagged as a reversal -- a clawback rather than a row that never existed.
No money moves: there is no gateway here that could send it, so this records the decision exactly as Orders.REFUNDED does.
